Best Starting Class in Elden Ring: Complete Breakdown

2026-07-27•10 min read

Choosing the Best Starting Class in Elden Ring

The class selection screen in Elden Ring can feel overwhelming. Ten classes, each with different stat spreads, starting gear, and implied playstyles. Picking the best starting class in Elden Ring is not about finding one objectively correct answer. It is about matching a class to the way you want to play the game. This guide breaks down every starting class, explains what each one excels at, and tells you which one you should pick based on your preferred style.

One thing to keep in mind before we dive in: there are no wrong choices here. Every class can complete the game. Every class can access every weapon, spell, and armor set. Your starting class shapes the first few hours of your journey, not the destination. With that said, some classes undeniably make the early game smoother than others.

The Top Tier: Best Elden Ring Starter Classes for Most Players

Vagabond — The Reliable Tank

If you want the single most beginner-friendly answer to "what is the best starting class in Elden Ring," the Vagabond is it. Here is why:

  • High Vigor and Strength from the start, meaning you can survive hits and swing heavy weapons effectively.
  • 100 percent physical block shield — the Halberd starting shield lets you block all physical damage when guarding, which is an enormous safety net while you learn enemy patterns.
  • Longsword and Halberd are both solid, versatile weapons that scale well into the mid-game.
  • Heavy armor gives you better poise, meaning enemies are less likely to stagger you when you get hit.

The Vagabond is the class we recommend for players who are new to FromSoftware games or who simply want a relaxed, methodical playstyle. You will not set speed records, but you will rarely feel helpless.

Early game tip: Head to the Coastal Cave immediately after reaching Limgrave to pick up the Uchigatana. It gives you a bleed weapon on top of the Vagabond's natural tankiness, and the combination is devastating.

Samurai — The Agile Striker

The Samurai is the best Elden Ring starter class for players who want fast, aggressive combat from the very beginning. The starting stats favor Dexterity and Arcane, and the starting equipment is phenomenal.

  • Uchigatana — one of the best early-game weapons in the game. Fast attacks, bleed buildup, and excellent Dexterity scaling. Many veteran players consider this weapon viable for the entire game.
  • Longbow — gives you a ranged option right from the start, which is useful for pulling enemies and finishing off low-health targets.
  • Medium armor with good poise — not as heavy as the Vagabond, but still protective enough to survive mistakes.
  • High Dexterity means your Uchigatana hits harder out of the gate than it would on most other classes.

The Samurai is ideal for players who enjoy dodge-heavy combat and want to feel powerful quickly. The Uchigatana carries you surprisingly far, and the bleed mechanic melts bosses that have enormous health pools.

Early game tip: Invest in Dexterity and Arcane to maximize the Uchigatana's bleed buildup. Grab the Bloody Slash Ash of War from the Iron Finger NPC to make the weapon even more lethal.

Astrologer — The Magic Powerhouse

If you want to obliterate enemies from a distance, the Astrologer is the best Elden Ring class for pure magical firepower. Sorcery in Elden Ring is incredibly strong, and the Astrologer starts with all the tools you need to make it work.

  • Glintstone Pebble and Arc — two sorceries right out of the gate. Pebble fires a fast projectile, and Arc sweeps a wide beam. Combined, they handle almost every early-game encounter.
  • Glintstone Staff — your casting tool, already in your inventory.
  • High Intelligence — means your sorceries hit harder from level one.
  • Good ranged playstyle — you can clear many encounters without ever being in melee range.

The Astrologer is excellent for players who enjoy a tactical, methodical approach to combat. You learn enemy patterns from a safe distance, pick your shots, and manage your FP (Focus Points) carefully.

Early game tip: Head to the Church of Elleh and buy theStars of Ruin sorcery from Kalé once you have enough runes. Also, grab the Meteorite Staff from the Street of Sages Ruins — it has S-rank Intelligence scaling and outclasses your starting staff for a significant portion of the game.

The Mid Tier: Viable but Demanding

Confessor — The Holy Warrior

The Confessor is a hybrid class that combines solid melee stats with healing and support incantations. It is a strong choice for players who want some magical utility without fully committing to a caster build.

  • Healing incantations let you recover health without using your flask, which is valuable in long fights.
  • Broadsword and shield provide reliable melee and defense.
  • Faith stat opens up fire, lightning, and holy damage options as you progress.

The Confessor is a solid Elden Ring starter class, but it requires a bit more build knowledge to excel than the three top-tier options. You need to decide early whether you are leaning more toward melee or magic, and invest accordingly.

Hero — The Strength Berserker

The Hero starts with massive Strength and a battle axe. It is the pure brute-force option, and it hits like a truck from the very start.

  • High Strength means heavy weapons are immediately usable and effective.
  • Battle Axe is a decent starting weapon, though most players swap it quickly.
  • Shield with decent block provides some defensive capability.

The Hero is fun if you want to smash things, but the low Dexterity and Arcane limit your weapon options early on. The Vagabond covers a similar niche with more survivability, which is why the Hero sits in the mid tier.

The Lower Tier: Niche Picks for Experienced Players

Prophet — The Faith Caster

The Prophet starts with high Faith and access to healing and fire incantations. It is the pure caster equivalent of the Astrologer, but faith-based magic is more support-oriented than the Astrologer's raw damage output. The Prophet is a niche pick that works best for players who specifically want a healing-focused or fire-focused build.

Bandit — The Critical Strike Specialist

The Bandit starts with high Arcane and a pair of daggers designed for critical hits and bleed buildup. It is a glass cannon with low Vigor and armor, but the damage output is explosive once you get the build rolling. We recommend the Bandit only for experienced players who understand how to manage aggro and positioning.

Wretch — The Blank Slate

The Wretch starts at level 1 with 10 in every stat and nothing but a club. It is the ultimate challenge class and a popular choice for experienced players who want to build their character from absolute scratch. For your first playthrough, the Wretch is unnecessarily punishing.

Prisoner — The Spellblade

The Prisoner blends Intelligence and Dexterity, offering a spellblade playstyle with sorcery and fast melee weapons. It is a compelling concept, but the starting stats are split enough that neither the magic nor the melee feels as strong as a dedicated class. Better for a second or third playthrough.

Which Class Should You Actually Pick?

Here is the short version of our complete breakdown:

  • First playthrough, want easy: Vagabond
  • First playthrough, want fast: Samurai
  • First playthrough, want magic: Astrologer
  • Second playthrough, want hybrid: Confessor or Prisoner
  • Challenge run: Wretch or Bandit

The best starting class in Elden Ring is the one that makes you excited to play. If the idea of swinging a colossal hammer appeals to you, pick the Hero. If you want to fling lightning from the sky, pick the Prophet. The game is long enough and flexible enough that any class can become anything. Pick what sounds fun, and the stats will follow.
